newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel shares end sharply down on Wall Street fall.
newsitem.headline: Israel shares end sharply down on Wall Street fall.

text.p: Israeli shares closed sharply lower on Sunday following Friday's steep plunge on Wall Street, traders said.

The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares fell 2.11 percent, or 6.36 points, to 295.00 on an all-share turnover of 165 million shekels against 120 million shekels on Thursday, the last day of trading before the Israeli weekend.
The Maof 25 blue-chip index closed 1.76 percent lower at 302.69.
Traders said the session opened with sharp declines and the indices fell by more than three percent, but towards the end of the day the market started recovering.
"We were expecting the market to fall today after Wall Street's decline. But this is no catastrophe and the market did not react too strongly," said Izik Winish at Capital Securities.
The Dow Jones industrial average sank 247 points on Friday in the second-biggest point loss in history.
"The trigger for today's decline was New York's decline. Wall Street dictates the behaviour of the local market," said Shahar Gazit at Ilanot Batucha.
Traders said that the market was not affected by the release of a relatively high July consumer price index (CPI) on Friday.
"The CPI was within expectations and the market prices reflected expectations for a rise of 1.1 percent," Winish said.
July CPI, released on Friday, rose 1.0 percent against a rise of 1.1 pct in June.
"Investors are only showing interest in Wall Street and the CPI did not affect trading. Analysts believe that the Bank of Israel will raise its key lending rate by 0.5 percentage point," Gazit said.
The base rate stands at 12.7 percent on an annual basis, where it has been since mid-June.
"Investors are waiting to see what will happen in New York on Monday. A further decline might send the local market downwards," Winish said.

Gazit added that the market was expected to remain quiet on Monday as investors waited for the opening of Wall Street. "Activity is expected to be relatively low on Monday. We are waiting for Wall Street and the focus is on the U.S. markets," Gazit said.

The most active shares were Bank Hapoalim, which lost 2.0 percent to 780 agorot (Israeli cents) on volume of 9.4 million shekels; Bank Leumi, which declined 1.75 percent to 576 agorot on turnover of 7.9 million shekels; and Agan Chemicals Manufacturers, which fell 3.0 percent to 9,120 agorot on volume of 6.2 million shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
